items.difficulty_reason: The counted lemma is the author lemma at source lines 1036-1040: the circle admits a partition into two disjoint sets, each of which partitions into countably many pieces that can be rotated to form a copy of the circle. The author proof (1042-1063) is a complete construction in three cited steps: split the rational rotation group into halves R_1 and R_2 as in the unit's disjoint-group lemma, define D_i as the union of the choice-set images rho(C) over R_i; the images form a partition of the circle with disjoint pieces by the unit's cover and no-overlap lemmas; and each family can be rotated to a copy of the circle because squaring maps R_i onto the whole rotation group (the disjoint-group lemma's content: theta maps to 2 theta is a bijection from the half-range onto the full range), so rotating each piece rho(C) by rho yields the family {(rho composed with rho)(C)} whose union is the circle by the cover lemma. The construction, the partition argument, and the reassembly identity are all present; the invoked lemmas are proved earlier in the same unit.
